-- title

Introducing NeoDoc

Hey folks! 

I'm Alan. I'd like to introduce you to 
NeoDoc. A writing format for the
Atmosphere^^1^^. 


-- footnote
-- id: 1

Well. NeoDoc was originally designed for my
static site generator. But, damned if it's 
not perfect the Atmosphere. 


-- comment

You're seeing the raw format right now. 
That's because the parser hasn't been 
integrated into the site yet. That's no 
problem. NeoDoc is designed to make it
easy to make content. A big part of
that is ensuring it's readable as
plain-text. 

It's like >>Markdown|
https://www.markdownguide.org/>>. 
But, you can do way more with it.

For example, when NeoDoc files
are transformed into web pages the
``-- comment`` sections are hidden. 
So, this note will automatically  
disappear when the parser is in place. 
Appropriate, since you'll no longer 
be seeing the raw text at that point. 


-- h2

How It Started

Three years ago, I hit my breaking point
with website tools. I was using 
Next.js^^next^^ and tried to correct a 
typo on my site. I changed a single
character and everything broke. Some
part of the process that built the site
simply stopped working. 

My site is 25 years old. I have no 
desire to deal with that shit for the 
next 25. So, I started building my own 
tools. Since I had a blank slate, I 
re-examined every aspect. That included 
using Markdown for content.


-- footnote
-- id: next

Look. I know lots of folks love 
>>Next|https://nextjs.org/>> and 
>>React|https://react.dev/>>.
They're just way overkill for what I 
do. The associated complexity causes 
more issue than I'm willing to deal with.


-- h2

Starting From Scratch

One of my favorite phrases is:


-- blockquote

Broken gets fixed. Shoddy is forever. 


-- p

As great as Markdown is for simple
blog posts, it sucks at making 
interesting pages. Anything beyond 
basic formatting and you have to roll 
to using HTML directly. 

For the longest time, I considred it
a shoddy experience. As I thought
about making content for the rest of 
my life, I realized it's broken^^3^^. 


-- footnote
-- id: 3

Or, at least, the wrong tool for the
job. When you can't do interesting things
in HTML without having to actually write
the HTML, it's not up to snuff. 


-- p

That realiztion started me down the path of 
desining a new content format. Something as 
easy to use as Markdown without sacraficing 
the power of the web's native language. 

Three years later, the result is NeoDoc. 


-- h2

Where It's At

The NeoDoc parser is currently embedded in
my static site generator. Extracting it
has been on the todo list forever. It just 
wasn't a priority. Folks would have to 
make new tools to use it. Not likely, 
given the quality of the established 
website building options. 

But, you know what doesn't have established
options? The Atmosphere. 

It's the Wild West. Harkenoning back to the 
early days of the web. Before everything got 
forced into the conformity of corporste, siloed 
social networks. 

We're at an epoch. Standardization is still 
under way. Once it takes hold, it'll be
impossible to overcome. If we're not careful, 
we'll end up with Markdown and siloed 
content again. 

It's up to us to make sure that doesn't
happen. To take our best shots at improving
things before they solidify. 


-- h2

Taking A Swing

And so, I'm offeing NeoDoc as a path 
forward. Not just for websites, but as 
an interoperatable format to underlie 
the Atmosphere. The Personal Data Servers 
of AT Proto give us control of our content. 
We can move what we make between apps
at our own volition. That's of little 
use if they all require differnet formats. 
The promise of freedom of movement is only 
avaialbe if movemnet requires no effort. 

That's what NeoDoc offers. The final
piece of puzzle to complete the vision
of the decentralized web. 

-a









-- endnote

I use NeoDoc on my personal site where
it's responsible for
>>three thousand or so pages|
https://www.alanwsmith.com/neo-files/report>>.
